violations.why: The ISR increments v_pylon between two reads of v_pylon used as an index, breaking atomicity.
The task writes v_vessel[2] (if v_pylon == 2) and later reads it, while the ISR can write the same element in between.
The task reads v_vessel[2] (if v_pylon == 2), the ISR may write that element, and the task reads it again, forming a read‑write‑read violation.
A write to v_vessel[2] by the task can be interleaved with the ISR’s write to the same element before the task reads it.
If the random index i equals 2, the task writes v_vessel[2], the ISR may write the same element, and the task later reads it, yielding a write‑write‑read violation.
